Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for India's reply. Charlie Dean leads her side out onto the park. It will be the left-hand, right-hand combination of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma to open the innings for India. Lauren Bell will kick things off with the new ball. Bell dismissed both Indian openers in the first over down in Chelmsford. Mandhana will take strike. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

England have all the momentum - It was a stop-start innings for the hosts as a few of their batters got in, but couldn't kick on. Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Amy Jones and even Alice Capsey all got starts but nothing substantial to show for it. It was Freya Kemp who made all the difference with a blistering unbeaten 39 off just 13 balls, and it is certainly game on heading into the chase. With 169 needed for the win, the Powerplay will be crucial for both sides. If the Indian openers manage to get off to a good start, this could turn into a humdinger. If England Women pick up early wickets, they will have the chance to dictate terms. Stay tuned, as the exciting run chase is up next.

Indian spinners dominate the first half - India Women managed to pick up wickets at regular intervals right throughout the first innings, but the final couple of overs have undone all the good work. Sree Charani ruled the roost as she picked up three wickets, and Shreyanka Patil also bowled really well, but Deepti Sharma seemed a bit off colour. Nandni Sharma and Arundhati Reddy, the two pacers did well up until the death and those 24 runs in the final over could turn out to be decisive.

England finish with a flourish - What hitting from Freya Kemp and right at the death, the hosts have stolen all the momentum away from India. For 18 overs, India Women were right on top of proceedings, but they will now have to bat pretty well to gun down this target of 169 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! It has been a fairly sedate first half of the innings from England. Amy Jones looks in good touch and will be keen to turn this start into something substantial. Expect India to lean heavily on their spin resources through the middle overs. The surface is a bit dry and a touch on the slower side, while the outfield is not the quickest either. How England navigate the spin challenge will go a long way towards determining the kind of total they end up with. Arundhati Reddy to bowl after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: Not in control but safe. Tossed up, full and around off. Wyatt-Hodge reaches out in front and attempts the sweep but the ball drops on her and a top edge is found. It goes fine of Yastika Bhatia at short fine leg and Danni comes back for the second run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Shreyanka Patil to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted delivery, on the fuller side. Wyatt-Hodge goes deep in the crease and glides it fine of the short third fielder with an open bat face. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Shreyanka Patil to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit too short, on middle. Sophia rocks back and pulls it to deep square leg. Just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Shreyanka Patil to Sophia Dunkley, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit of turn first up for Patil. On a length, spinning back in at the pads. Dunkley stabs it down from the crease.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Shreyanka Patil to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shreyanka Patil comes in as the first bowling change.
Near the tramline, on a back of a length. Sophia throws her hands at the ball but mistimes it to the left of cover-point. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dug in short by Reddy, outside off. Dunkley is happy to let it go.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Reddy drags the length back now, on middle. Sophia hangs back to defend.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Clean strike! Reddy hurls it full and outside off. Dunkley hangs low and reaches out to drag it over mid on. She connects well and manages to clear the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Just short! Reddy continues to be full, around off. Wyatt-Hodge extends her hands out in front and plays an uppish drive. It does not carry to Smriti Mandhana at cover and she collects it on the bounce. Mandhana spots Dunkley being out of the crease and she takes her chance. She misses her shy at the bowling end and the ball rolls towards deep mid-wicket, allowing a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arundhati Reddy to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swinging back in at the pads, on a length. Danni presses onto the front foot for the flick but misses and wears it on the front pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Arundhati Reddy to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Arundhati Reddy to continue...
Short and wide on off by Sharma, Wyatt-Hodge reaches out and slaps it to deep backward point for just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Nandni Sharma to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the top of off, does Nandni. Wyatt-Hodge hangs on the back foot and stays leg side of the ball before steering it to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Nandni Sharma to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sharma sprays it on the pads, on a good length. Sophia nudges it behind square leg and turns the strike over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Nandni Sharma to Sophia Dunkley, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angled in, on a short of a length, on middle. Wyatt-Hodge drops it with soft hands beside the strip on the off side and hurries to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Nandni Sharma to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on off, Dunkley slams it hard to cover, where Shafali Verma does well to get low and makes a half-stop. The batters cross as the ball goes away to Verma's left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Nandni Sharma to Sophia Dunkley, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! It is Jemimah Rodrigues of all people. That should have been taken. A hint of away shape, on a back of a length. Dunkley's eyes light up as she sees the width on offer. She slaps it hard but can't keep it down. Hits it uppishly to backward point, where Rodrigues leaps and gets her hands out in front of her face to take the catch. The ball hits her on the palm and drops to the ground.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Nandni Sharma to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nandni Sharma to operate from the other end.
Sliding onto the pads, on the fuller side. Wyatt-Hodge misses out on the glance. The ball dribbles to short fine leg off her pads. A quiet start to the game. Just 2 runs off the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arundhati Reddy to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Honing in on the off stump, on a nagging length. Danni dabs it from the crease to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arundhati Reddy to Danni Wyatt-Hodge, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Reddy drifts down leg, on a good length. Richa Ghosh is standing up to the stumps and she moves to her left but fails to gather the ball cleanly. It deflects towards short third off her gloves, and the batters cross over. England are underway.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, 2 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and tight from Reddy. Bowled on a good length and keeps the stumps in play. Dunkley presents a straight bat to keep it out. Four dots in a row to start with.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated up by Reddy, swinging back into the pads. Dunkley brings her bat out in front and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags the length back a bit and it tails back in sharply into the right-hander. Sophia turns it off the pads towards short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Arundhati finds a bit of inward shape up front. Keeps it nice and full, attacking the sticks. Dunkley watchfully blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Arundhati Reddy to Sophia Dunkley, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin. The umpires are out in the middle, and so are the players of India Women. It will be the pairing of Sophia Dunkley and Danni Wyatt-Hodge to open the innings for England Women. Arundhati Reddy has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Yastika Bhatia, Harmanpreet Kaur (C) (In for Bharti Fulmali), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil (In for Kranti Gaud), Sree Charani and Nandni Sharma.

England Women (Playing XI) - Sophia Dunkley, Danni Wyatt-Hodge (In for Issy Wong), Amy Jones (WK), Alice Capsey, Heather Knight, Freya Kemp, Danielle Gibson, Charlie Dean (C), Sophie Ecclestone, Linsey Smith (In for Tilly Corteen-Coleman) and Lauren Bell.
TOSS - Harmanpreet Kaur is back to lead India. The flip of the coin lands in favour of Charlie Dean. England elect to BAT first.

Top-order conundrum - Despite securing a vital 1-0 lead, India's team management faces a glaring conundrum following the unexpected failure of their elite opening combination. While early dismissals exposed the top order, it forced a remarkable rescue mission that put India's incredible squad depth on full display. However, relying solely on the middle and lower order to bail the team out remains a high-risk gamble against a wounded English bowling attack. Heading into this second T20I, India’s primary objective will be to restore rhythm at the top, marrying solid Powerplay aggression with technical stability to set up their batting effort. Toss and team news to follow...

England's tactical calibration - For the host nation, the opening defeat serves as a sharp wake-up call that exposes critical vulnerabilities ahead of this must-win fixture. While England Women showcased flashes of individual brilliance, their overall execution lacked the cohesive sting needed to suffocate a rampant Indian lineup. The hosts stumbled heavily during the middle overs, where a stagnant strike rotation and a lack of steady partnerships allowed pressure to mount, triggering avoidable wickets. To level the series, England's experienced core must immediately recalibrate, demanding tighter bowling discipline at the death and a calculated, aggressive counter-attack from their explosive batting unit.

India's blueprint - The series opener belonged entirely to India Women, who brought their absolute A-game to lay down a massive marker for their World Cup preparation. Defeating a formidable English side in their own backyard is a monumental challenge, but the Women in Blue displayed exceptional tactical discipline and collective resilience to outplay the hosts. Their clinical performance highlighted a fearless middle-order assault and an incredibly adaptive bowling plan, proving that India's structural blueprint is peaking at the perfect time. By seizing the early momentum, the visitors have unlocked a vital psychological edge and demonstrated the sheer squad depth required to dismantle elite opposition under intense pressure.

Blockbuster sequel - Welcome, cricket fans, to the high-stakes second chapter of the three-match T20I series between England Women and India Women. The atmosphere is bound to be electric as these two global powerhouses collide in a summer spectacle driven by a passionate worldwide fanbase. With the ICC Women's T20 World Cup fast approaching, this bilateral face-off has transformed into a critical testing ground where experiments meet raw ambition. Every run and tactical masterstroke carries immense weight, serving as a definitive dress rehearsal for global supremacy.
... MATCHDAY ...

Final preparations begin to intensify - The caravan now moves to Bristol, a venue that has traditionally belonged to England Women, five wins in six T20Is here underline just how comfortable they are in these conditions. Yet the one blemish on that record came against India last year, a reminder that this Indian side has already shown it can silence English crowds on this ground. But beyond the scoreline and the series lead, there is a much bigger narrative quietly shaping this contest. With the T20 World Cup in England now just around the corner, every innings, every bowling spell and every team selection suddenly carries extra significance. This is no longer just about winning a bilateral series, it is about discovering the combinations capable of surviving pressure when the global tournament begins on these very shores later this year. India's combination finally looks settled - India Women arrive in Bristol with several positives beginning to click into place at once. Smriti Mandhana stepped into the captaincy role confidently in the absence of Harmanpreet Kaur, who is expected to return for this game and strengthen an already dangerous middle order. Jemimah Rodrigues looked back to her fluent best in the opener, blending timing with controlled aggression, while Yastika Bhatia's comeback instantly added balance at the top. Add the firepower of Shafali Verma and Richa Ghosh, and India suddenly possess a batting lineup capable of matching England shot for shot in their own conditions. But perhaps the bigger story has been the emergence of India's younger bowling group. Nandni Sharma continues to justify the hype surrounding her after a breakthrough WPL season with a three-fer on debut, while Kranti Gaud and Sree Charani have added freshness and fearlessness to the attack. Alongside the experience of Deepti Sharma and Radha Yadav, India finally seem closer to building the kind of balanced T20 attack they have long searched for ahead of a World Cup. England need their senior players to step up - England Women, meanwhile, know Bristol better than most sides in world cricket, and they will expect a much sharper performance here. Amy Jones showed resilience in the first game, but the hosts need far more from their star names. Sophia Dunkley and Alice Capsey remain central to England's plans as an aggressive opening pair, while Heather Knight's experience becomes even more important with Nat Sciver-Brunt still unavailable. Also, they could bring back Danni Wyatt-Hodge to give them more balance up top. There were still positives for England despite the defeat. Tilly Corteen-Coleman impressed on debut with her control and composure under pressure, while Lauren Bell once again looked threatening with the new ball. Sophie Ecclestone, however, endured a rare off-night, and England could look towards the in-form Linsey Smith to strengthen the spin department after her excellent domestic season. Charlie Dean's consistency in the middle overs also remains crucial on a Bristol surface where one quiet spell can completely shift momentum. Form (Last 5 completed matches, recent first) - ENG - LWLWW | IND - WLWLL. Another high-scoring contest? The Bristol County Ground has built a reputation as one of the better batting venues in women's cricket in England. The short straight boundaries, quick outfield and generally true surface encourage attacking cricket, and totals above 170 are rarely safe here if dew settles in later. India know that from last year's win at this venue, while England's dominant record here reflects how dangerous they can become once momentum swings their way. With the World Cup approaching rapidly, both teams know strong performances now could shape not just this series, but their plans for the biggest tournament of the year.
